newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales up 1.0 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales up 1.0 pct in August.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK retail sales in August.
RETAIL SALES VOLUME AUGUST JULY JULY(PREL)
Market forecasts had centred on a 0.5 percent rise in retail sales on the month and a year-on-year increase of 3.5 percent.
BY SECTOR (percentage gain, minus indicates fall)
The average weekly non-seasonally adjusted value of retail sales in August was 3.09 billion stg, 6.0 percent up on August 1995.
In value terms, retail sales rose by 6.4 percent in the three months to end August on the same period a year earlier.
The ONS said the three-month-on-three month increase in retail sales volume in August was the highest since Aug 1988.
It said it was non-food retail sales that continued to drive the index higher.
* The three-month-on-three month increase in textile, clothing and footwear was the highest in 10 years.
